record.paper_title: Selected Open Problems in Continuous-Time Quantum Walks
record.context_brief: Uniform mixing and roots of unity
record.original_question: Let G be a graph with adjacency matrix A and transition matrix U(t)=exp(itA). Say that G admits instantaneous uniform mixing at time τ if all entries of U(τ) have the same absolute value, equivalently if all entries of the mixing matrix M(τ)=U(τ)∘U(-τ) are equal. Prove that whenever G admits uniform mixing at time τ, every eigenvalue of U(τ) is a root of unity.

evidence.quote: We say that G admits instantaneous uniform mixing (or simply uniform mixing) at time τ if all entries of M(τ) are equal. Equivalently, G admits uniform mixing at time τ if all entries of U(τ) have the same absolute value.
If G admits uniform mixing at time τ, then the eigenvalues of U(τ) are roots of unity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite simple graph with adjacency matrix A (a real symmetric 0/1 matrix). For t ∈ ℝ, define the unitary transition matrix U(t) = exp(itA) and the mixing matrix M(t) = U(t) ∘ U(−t), where ∘ denotes the entrywise (Hadamard) product; equivalently, M(t) is the matrix whose (u,v) entry is |U(t)_{u,v}|^2. Say that G admits instantaneous uniform mixing at time τ ∈ ℝ if all entries of M(τ) are equal (equivalently, all entries of U(τ) have the same absolute value 1/√n, where n is the number of vertices of G).

Prove or disprove: whenever G admits instantaneous uniform mixing at some time τ, every eigenvalue of the unitary matrix U(τ) is a root of unity.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture appears in a recent survey of open problems on continuous-time quantum walks and is listed as an open problem. Partial results are known: for integral abelian Cayley graphs and several restricted families, the conclusion has been established via Kronecker-type arguments, but a general proof is not available in the literature.

status_evidence.snippet: Listed as an open problem regarding uniform mixing and roots of unity.
status_evidence.claim: The statement is posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Uniform mixing on integral abelian Cayley graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Using Kronecker's theorem, the time at which integral abelian Cayley graphs admit uniform mixing yields eigenvalues that are roots of unity.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist for integral abelian Cayley graphs.
